channel.title: Megajournal Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from the multidisciplinary megajournals: Nature Communications, restricted to biological and health sciences, and Science Advances, which is not filtered by subject because no accessible source exposes one.

item.title: Nature Communications: Hypothalamic prolactin receptor + dopaminergic neurons regulate energy metabolism and nociceptive threshold in mice during lactation
item.description: The mechanisms by which the brain controls maternal metabolism through hormones remain unclear. Here, authors find PRLR + dopaminergic neurons in the hypothalamus regulate bone and fat metabolism and alter nociceptive threshold through NPY in lactating mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Commensal bacteria inhibit viral infections via a tryptophan metabolite
item.description: Previous studies suggest that commensal bacteria modulate viral infections. Here, the authors use HIV as a model to show that commensal bacteria impact viral infections, pinpointing a specific tryptophan metabolite as a key player.

item.title: Nature Communications: Modulating pressure in the Orbitrap improves sensitivity and mass resolution in charge detection mass spectrometry
item.description: Orbitrap-based single-ion charge mass spectrometry of biomolecular assemblies can be hampered by gas-induced ion losses. Here, the authors introduce a pulsed valve to regulate vacuum conditions resulting in improved ion detection enabling sensitive, accurate, and higher-resolution mass measurements

Nature Communications: Cooperation, competition and enforcement in transposon evolution
item.description: Transposons are genetic parasites that have had far-reaching effects on eukaryotic evolution. This modelling study shows that host defences against transposon activity are necessary to prevent species extinction.

item.title: Nature Communications: Inflammatory neuropathy in mouse and primate models of colorectal cancer
item.description: Whether cancer damages peripheral nerves before treatment is unclear. Here, authors show that colorectal tumors drive inflammation and disrupt neuronal lipids, causing subtle sensory pathology in mice and monkeys that may persist in survivors.

item.title: Nature Communications: Identification and validation of a previously missed mutational signature in colorectal cancer
item.description: Mutational signature SBS_D had been previously identified in a large-scale genomics analysis of microsatellite-stable colorectal cancers (CRC), and had been decomposed into known mutational signatures. Here, the authors demonstrate in data from three CRC cohorts that SBS_D is an independent mutational signature that may be linked to DNA repair infidelity, and is now designated as SBS111.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multiple-layer mesh from electrospinnable amyloid‑like protein and their application in treating oral ulcer
item.description: Dynamic moist conditions limit oral ulcer patch performance. Here, authors build amyloid-like protein meshes via unfolding-stabilization for wet adhesion and faster healing.

item.title: Nature Communications: TDP-43 controls RNA structure through high affinity lattice interactions
item.description: TDP-43 is an essential RNA-binding protein. Here, the authors show how it binds single-stranded poly(UG) RNA through high affinity 1D lattice interactions. The N-terminal domain functions to accelerate association and dissociation rates through inter and intramolecular protein interactions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Loss-of-function mutation in Omicron variants reduces spike protein expression and attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection
item.description: Spike mutations in SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants impact vaccine-mediated protection. In this study, the authors identify mutations that also alter spike cleavage and virus entry and that these Omicron mutations reshape both pathogenesis and transmission outcomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: ARID5A RNA-binding coordinates microglial defense and ferroptosis in iPSC-derived models
item.description: RNA-binding proteins shape gene expression, but their roles in brain immune cells are unclear. Here, the authors show that ARID5A regulates RNA processing in microglia, linking immune and lysosomal pathways to iron-driven death in neurodegeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structure and mechanism of human sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter MFSD2B
item.description: Sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) is a potent lipid signaling molecule. Here, the authors determine the cryo-EM structures of the erythrocyte and platelet S1P transporter MFSD2B from humans. Combining the structural, biochemical, and computational analyses, the authors reveal the molecular basis of S1P recognition and transport by MFSD2B in hematopoietic cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Large-scale admixture mapping in the All of Us Research Program improves the characterization of cross-population phenotypic differences
item.description: In this work, Mandla et al. identified >50 genetic loci where ancestry was associated with a trait, expanding on the underlying biological mechanisms of these traits and the potential genetic factors of their differences between populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: IL-2 mutein-engrafted antibody MHS552 selectively expands functional regulatory T cells in nonclinical models and healthy participants
item.description: Although low-dose IL-2 therapy has shown promise in treating autoimmune and inflammatory conditions by supporting the expansion and immunosuppressive activity of regulatory T cells (Treg), robust clinical responses have been lacking. Here, the authors describe the design of the Treg-selective IL-2 agonist MHS552, its preclinical characterization in non-human primates, and a first-in-human dose escalation study in healthy participants reporting efficacy, selectivity and safety of the IL-2 mutein.

item.title: Nature Communications: Prefrontal-raphe-habenular circuit drives fear memory recall and updating
item.description: Fear memory recall is a vital defensive response, but its neuronal mechanism remains unclear. Here, authors show a brainstem pathway that links memory centers to negative emotional states during fear memory recall, showing how the brain reactivates fear in the absence of danger.

item.title: Nature Communications: Amiloride mitigates respiratory distress caused by WFDC2 deficiency via inhibiting the epithelial sodium channel
item.description: This study identifies a WFDC2 mutation that causes a severe cystic-fibrosis-like airway disease in humans and mice. The mutation overactivates the epithelial sodium channel, and treatment with the drug amiloride improves survival and lung function in affected mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: A foundation model for acute abdomen diagnosis stratification and triage on noncontrast computed tomography
item.description: The authors present AbdomenNet, a foundation model for non-contrast computed tomography. It detects 11 acute abdominal conditions, helps identify high-risk cases, improves radiologist accuracy, and may speed emergency reporting.

item.title: Nature Communications: Zinc displacement and metabolic interference: cobalt ion-mediated therapy for broad-spectrum CRKP-resistant pneumonia via inhalable microspheres
item.description: The global rise of carbapenem-resistant bacteria, driven by enzymes such as KPC-2 and OXA-48 as well as metallo-β-lactamases, poses a major challenge to antibiotic therapy. Here, the authors develop a cobalt-based microsphere platform for the delivery of meropenem, leveraging Co²⁺ as a metal-based resistance breaker to overcome multiple resistance mechanisms. In a mouse model of drug-resistant pneumonia, the treatment improved survival, reduced bacterial burden, and mitigated excessive inflammation, highlighting a promising strategy for combating multidrug-resistant infections.

item.title: Nature Communications: Youth-associated protein TIMP2 regulates microglial state and function in healthy and aged mice
item.description: Aging disrupts microglial function, but factors that rejuvenate these cells are poorly characterized. Here, the authors show the youth-associated protein TIMP2 revitalizes microglia by altering inflammatory states and restoring phagocytosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Subclinical exposure to Streptococcus pyogenes drives the development of long-lived homologous immunity
item.description: The rate of infection with Streptococcus pyogenes reduces with age and is thought to be driven at least in part due to immunity derived from repeated exposure during life. Here the authors using data from human challenge studies and animal models of infection, suggest subclinical exposure to S.pyogenes results in long lived homologous immunity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Photostimulation improves maturation of human photoreceptors
item.description: Human retinal organoids can be taught to “see”: rhythmic light stimulation enhances photoreceptor maturation, strengthens retinal connectivity and improves functional responses, revealing light as a developmental signal for the human retina.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bony labyrinth morphology reveals deep population history and isolation among Homo sapiens in prehistoric northeastern Africa (44–3 ka)
item.description: Little is known of the Homo sapiens population history in late prehistoric northeastern Africa. Using inner ear morphology from 148 individuals, this study documents 40.000 years of human evolution, interactions and isolation in these groups.

item.title: Nature Communications: A systematic identification of resistance determinants to antisense antibiotics suggests adaptation strategies dependent on the delivery peptide
item.description: In this study, authors investigate the evolution of bacterial resistance to antisense peptide nucleic acid (PNA) antibiotics. They observe that this typically occurs mainly by reducing drug uptake via mutations in the carrier peptide’s transporter, while resistance to a different carrier peptide stayed low and is easily bypassed by tweaking the drug sequence.

item.title: Nature Communications: Population-based genomic detection of childhood cancer predisposition using newborn dried blood spots
item.description: Prospective genomic newborn screening in large populations with extended follow-ups are necessary to assess the impact of the inclusion of cancer genes on outcomes. Here, the authors show that newborn screening for germline cancer risk, using a limited panel of cancer predisposition genes, would identify the approximately 1/27,000 babies who will develop a cancer in the first eight years of life due to a cancer predisposition syndrome, including nearly all children who go on to develop bilateral retinoblastoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Peritoneal ovarian cancer growth in the omentum proceeds independently of mature adipocytes
item.description: Ovarian cancer (OC) often spreads to the omentum, an adipose-rich tissue in the abdomen. Here, authors show that FABP4-expressing endothelial cells contribute to OC growth in the omentum independently of mature adipocytes.

item.title: Nature Communications: A flexible repertoire of wound closure strategies precedes whole-body regeneration
item.description: Animals capable of whole-body regeneration can heal virtually any wound. Here they show that Hofstenia miamia accomplishes this feat through variable morphogenetic strategies that depend on which epithelial layers are damaged, revealing a versatile toolkit for repair.

item.title: Nature Communications: Host-aware Identification of Intrinsic Gene Expression Biopart Parameters using Combinatorial Libraries
item.description: Model-based design in synthetic biology is limited because bioparts are typically characterised by relative metrics that vary across genetic and physiological contexts. Here, using combinatorial libraries of plasmid-based expression constructs and a host-aware E. coli digital twin, the authors identify intrinsic biopart parameters that provide a basis for more predictive model-based design of synthetic gene circuits.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ultra-sensitive profiling of CRISPR-Cas off-target effects with Tracking-seq2
item.description: Ensuring safe gene editing requires precise detection of unintended DNA edits. Here, authors develop Tracking-seq2, a highly sensitive method to profile off-targets for diverse genome editors, and reveal distinct off-target effects across individuals in primary human cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Integrative structural analysis of human endosomal NHE6 reveals a lipid-associated gate and disordered C-terminus
item.description: The endosomal Na+ /H+ exchanger HsNHE6 regulates organellar pH and is implicated in neurological disease. Here the authors determine its cryo-EM structure and show a kinetic preference for K+ over Na+ transport.

item.title: Nature Communications: APOBEC3-driven attenuation of the 2022 global outbreak monkeypox virus relative to its clade IIb ancestor
item.description: Here, the authors compare the ancestral MPXV A.1 and 2022 outbreak lineage B.1. They show that APOBEC3-driven mutations attenuate viral spread, immune evasion and virulence of B.1. Despite similar cell-culture replication, B.1 was less pathogenic in vivo, highlighting APOBEC3 as a potential driver of MPXV evolution.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ectomesenchymal identity emerges via relief of Twist1 transcript destabilisation
item.description: Here they identify a Twist1 enhancer that is activated early in the migrating cranial neural crest but the Twist1 3' UTR contains a vertebrate-specific AU-rich element that destabilises transcripts until ventral head signals relieve the repression, thereby gating ectomesenchymal identity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Towards efficient perturbation for the noncoding genome
item.description: The noncoding genome includes key regulatory elements, yet functional dissection remains challenging. Here, authors benchmarked five CRISPR-based perturbation tools and developed a deep learning model to guide pgRNA design, providing a practical framework for decoding noncoding genome function.

item.title: Nature Communications: Low kinetochore-microtubule occupancy leaves a mitotic memory by delaying checkpoint silencing
item.description: How do cells faithfully segregate chromosomes within an optimal time? Using naturally “super-resolved” kinetochores, the authors show that maximal microtubule occupancy prevents bad mitotic memories to ensure proliferation of the next generations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Dissecting root-specific non-conventional effector-triggered immunity and its role in defense and shifting the microbiome
item.description: Roots, unlike leaves, are continuously exposed to a complex soil microbiome. Here the authors reveal root-specific effector-triggered immune responses distinct from those in leaves.

item.title: Nature Communications: Widespread horizontal transfer and strong selection enhance microbial adaptation in Antarctic soils
item.description: Antarctica was long thought to be biologically static, but its microbial life is now known to be diverse and active. This study shows that widespread horizontal gene transfer and purifying selection drive microbial adaptation in Antarctic soils.

item.title: Nature Communications: ESMDynamic: Fast and accurate prediction of protein dynamic contact maps from single sequences
item.description: Predicting protein dynamics from sequence remains challenging. Here, authors introduce ESMDynamic, an AI model that rapidly predicts contact fluctuations, providing insights that can reduce reliance on physics-based simulations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Segment any tumour: an uncertainty-aware vision foundation model for whole-body analysis
item.description: The application of prompt-driven vision foundation models to medical imaging, particularly whole-body tumour analysis, remains challenging. Here, the authors develop Segment Any Tumour 3D (SAT3D), a lightweight volumetric foundation model for robust and generalisable tumour segmentation across diverse medical imaging modalities, organs, and cohorts.

item.title: Nature Communications: A modular self-assembling peptide platform targeting TGF-β1 for tendon regeneration
item.description: Excessive TGF-β1 activity contributes to tendon degeneration and fibrosis. Here, authors develop a self-assembling peptide that locally sequesters TGF-β1, restores tendon structure and function in rat and beagle models, and offers a strategy for treating fibrotic disorders.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatial and functional specialization of human splenic innate lymphoid cells
item.description: To date, the spatial and functional characterization of human splenic innate lymphoid cells (ILC) has remained limited. Here, the authors integrate CITE-seq and spatial transcriptomic data and present an atlas of human splenic NK and ILC cells and define high-resolution subset-specific spatial organization and interaction networks, providing insights into the presence of local immune niches in secondary lymphoid organs.

item.title: Nature Communications: In vitro reconstitution of chromatin replication recapitulates symmetric histone recycling
item.description: Symmetric recycling of parental histones to newly replicated DNA is vital for maintaining cell identity. Repli pore-seq reveals the reconstitution of this process from purified proteins, providing an in vitro system for studying parental histone recycling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Intrinsic and non-cell-autonomous roles for the neurodevelopmental syndrome-linked transcription factor UNC-3/EBF
item.description: The non-cell-autonomous functions of transcription factors in neuronal development remain poorly understood. Here, the authors show that UNC-3, the C. elegans homolog of the neurodevelopmental disorder gene EBF3 , regulates not only the development of UNC-3–expressing neurons but also that of neighboring neurons, revealing previously unrecognized mechanisms of neural circuit assembly.

item.title: Nature Communications: CAKR: commutative algebra k-mer representations for genomics
item.description: Comparative genomic analysis remains a fundamental challenge in genomics, genetics and phylogenetics, motivating the development of new mathematical frameworks for sequence comparison. The authors introduce a commutative algebra k-mer representation that integrates concepts from algebra, topology, combinatorics and machine learning, and evaluate its application to genetic variant classification, phylogenetic tree reconstruction and viral classification.

item.title: Nature Communications: Natural variation in BRN1 enhances nitrogen sensitivity to improve rice nitrogen use efficiency
item.description: Here the authors show that BRN1 is a core gene modulating nitrogen-dependent growth in rice. They identify favorable BRN1 alleles that can improves rice nitrogen use efficiency and grain yield and are potentially valuable for low-nitrogen rice breeding.

item.title: Nature Communications: Adipocyte-derived β-hydroxybutyrate confers metabolic resilience in multiple myeloma
item.description: Multiple cell populations within the bone tumour microenvironment have been shown to support multiple myeloma (MM). Here, the authors show that under glucose deprived conditions, adipocytes produce β-hydroxybutyrate, which promotes MM cell survival.

item.title: Nature Communications: Th17 effector cytokines induce shared and distinct microglial and endothelial cell responses in a mouse model for post-streptococcal encephalitis
item.description: Group A Streptococcus (GAS) infections can cause neuropsychiatric symptoms in children, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that IL-17A–IL17RA signaling in microglia mediates blood brain barrier dysfunction and neuroinflammation after GAS infection in a mouse model.

item.title: Nature Communications: Heart rate control by listening to light
item.description: The auditory-cardiac interplay allows sound to influence cardiac rhythm, but precise control is limited by acoustic wave propagation. Here, the authors present an opto-mechano-cardiac coupling strategy that uses optical traps to convert music rhythm into programmable otolith oscillations, identifying key neural pathways and successfully rescuing drug-induced arrhythmias.

item.title: Nature Communications: Synergistic magneto-enzymatic propulsion enables multimodal nanomotor swarms
item.description: Enzyme-powered nanomotors are primarily studied as individual particles with limited understanding of their collective behaviors, especially in three-dimensional and interface-dependent environments. This study reports a mechanistic proof-of-principle for a two-step multimodal nanomotor swarm that combines magnetic localization with catalysis-triggered interfacial expansion, elucidating the physical conditions governing their collective dynamics.

item.title: Nature Communications: Thalamocortical bursts encode reward contingencies and drive associative learning
item.description: Researchers find that brief high-frequency bursts of neural firing in mouse thalamus and cortex track the value of sensory cues during learning and invert their stimulus selectivity in response to task rule inversions. They further show suppressing these bursts impairs learning.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structure of NHE6 and its lipid-mediated interactions regulating endosomal pH
item.description: The sodium-proton exchanger NHE6 localises to endosomal membranes and mutations in the protein are known to cause the X-linked neurological disorder Christianson syndrome. Here the authors report four cryo-EM structures of rat NHE6, revealing its homodimeric structure, ion binding and remodelling by lipids.

item.title: Nature Communications: UNCOVERseq enables sensitive and controlled gene editing off-target nomination across CRISPR-Cas modalities and systems
item.description: CRISPR gene editing promises new therapies but raises concerns about unintended changes. Here, authors present UNCOVERseq, an in-cell method that sensitively detects rare off-target edits, benchmarks performance across editors, and improves risk assessment in therapeutic cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mechanism of K63-linked polyubiquitin recognition and cleavage by the BRCA1-A complex
item.description: How the BRCA1-A complex finds and removes ubiquitin signals at DNA breaks remains unknown. Here the authors show that ARISC–RAP80 binds K63-linked ubiquitin chains through multiple subunits and non-catalytic sites, revealing a coordinated ‘read-and-erase’ mechanism that guides DNA-damage repair.

item.title: Nature Communications: PA200 modulates immunoproteasome structure and activity
item.description: Proteasomes help cells recycle proteins and shape immune responses. Here, the authors show that PA200 binds strongly to the immunoproteasome, reshaping its structure and activity to alter generation of immune-related protein fragments.

item.title: Nature Communications: A ubiquitin chain-feeding mechanism for BRCA1-A
item.description: The BRCA1-A complex cleaves K63-linked polyubiquitin chains at DNA damage sites to control DNA repair. Here, the authors develop a polyubiquitin activity probe and present cryo-EM structures of BRCA1-A bound to it, revealing how avidity and processivity make BRCA1-A a chain-shortening enzyme.

item.title: Nature Communications: Blood metabolomic signatures linking air pollution to lung cancer in the Cancer Prevention Studies
item.description: Exposure to ambient air pollution is an established risk factor for lung cancer. In here, the authors report multiple metabolic perturbations that may mediate the association between ambient air pollution exposure and lung cancer risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neutrophil extracellular traps promote liver metastasis by impairing NK cell-dependent tumor surveillance via CCDC25
item.description: The formation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) contributes to liver metastasis and immune suppression. Here the authors show that NET-derived DNA can be sensed by CCDC25 on natural killer (NK) cells impairing NK cell-dependent tumor surveillance and promoting liver metastasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chronic conditions and aortic disease risk: a prospective cohort study with predictive and etiological analyses
item.description: This study shows that multimorbidity and several chronic conditions, including cardiovascular, respiratory and kidney diseases, are associated with higher risk of aortic disease in two large cohorts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Noninvasive 3D mapping of tissue stress using reverberant shear wave
item.description: Mechanical stress shapes soft tissue health, but imaging it non-invasively in vivo has remained a challenge. Here, authors used physics-informed MRI wave analysis to map 3D tissue stress, enabling non-invasive intracranial pressure and tumor-induced stress estimates in brain tumor patients.

item.title: Nature Communications: Automatic value learning results in counterproductive human behavior
item.description: Humans use rewards to learn which actions are worth repeating. Here, the authors demonstrate an automatic tendency to credit unrelated actions for these rewards, driving suboptimal choices.

item.title: Nature Communications: Immune niche composed of C1Q + macrophages/SFRP2 + CAFs/CD8 + T cells drives immunotherapy response in HER2-positive gastric cancer
item.description: HER2-positive gastric cancers represent a distinct subtype of the disease showing favourable response to combination therapy involving HER2 targeting and immune checkpoint blockade immunotherapy. Here the authors show by spatial transcriptomics and single-cell RNA sequencing that HER2 positivity associates with a favourable immune microenvironment that also determines their better response to immunotherapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Oxidative stress triggers RNAPII arrest through PARylation and DNA damage
item.description: Oxidative stress induces a rapid global transcription shutdown. Here, the authors show that RNAPII stops dead in its tracks. As transcription recovers, gene body–stalled RNAPII resumes transcription in a DNA repair–dependent manner, while early gene body RNAPII stalling is controlled by PARylation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genomic and genetic dissection underlying seedling drought resilience in oats
item.description: Drought severely constrains common oat production. By generating genome assemblies for oat accessions with contrasting drought tolerance, the authors identify genetic variants and candidate genes underlying drought resistance, including an NF-Y transcription factor and its putative upstream regulator.

item.title: Nature Communications: MALT1 protease inhibition restrains glioblastoma progression by reversing tumor-associated macrophage-dependent immunosuppression in mice
item.description: MALT1 protease is an intracellular signalling molecule that regulates adaptive immune responses and has been implicated in the pathogenesis of hematologic and solid malignancies. Here, the authors investigate the function of MALT1 in tumor-associated macrophages. In preclinical models of glioblastoma (GBM), tumor cells induce MALT1 and NFKb signaling activation, driving macrophage polarization towards a tumor-supportive phenotype, and MALT1 inhibition enhances macrophage immunoreactivity, suppressing GBM tumor growth.

item.title: Nature Communications: Suppression of transcription-replication conflicts by sequence-coordinated actions of TRDMT1 and MutLα
item.description: DNA strand break repair can be assisted by RNA dependent mechanism. Here the authors show that the RNA methyltransferase TRDMT1 and the mismatch repair complex MutLα independently recognize DNA-RNA hybrids and cooperatively suppress co-transcriptional R-loops, with m5C directing pathway choice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Enhancing pan-cancer spatial transcriptomics at single-cell resolution with stPainter
item.description: This study presents stPainter, a pan-cancer pretrained model that enhances sparse spatial transcriptomics data and supports analysis of cellular organization across tumor tissues without matched single-cell references.

item.title: Nature Communications: Transcriptomic analysis of spinal V1 interneurons informs their multifunctional role in motor output
item.description: This study leverages transcriptomic profiling of spinal V1 interneurons to understand how they contribute to movement. By genetically targeting and manipulating these neurons, the authors decouple locomotor speed and limb flexion phenotypes, suggesting these key elements of motor control may be governed by different subsets of V1 interneurons.

item.title: Nature Communications: Rab4b controls hepatic glucose production during fasting through glycophagy
item.description: This study reveals an unexpected role for Rab4b-dependent endocytic recycling in orchestrating the liver’s response to fasting, linking autophagy-driven glycogen breakdown to glucose production.

item.title: Nature Communications: Pseudomonas aeruginosa -derived volatile organic compounds modulate AhR signaling to dysregulate airway mucus homeostasis
item.description: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) produced by Pseudomonas aeruginosa are potential biomarkers for diagnosing acute exacerbation in diseased lungs. Kuo et al. reveal that VOCs activate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor to exacerbate airway mucus pathology.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evidence of dengue transmission and a diverse Aedes mosquito virome on the Congo’s Angola border
item.description: Mosquito sequencing along the DRC-Angola border reveals diverse viruses and evidence of ongoing dengue transmission. This study shows that xenosurveillance has the potential to improve emerging infectious disease detection and prevention.

item.title: Nature Communications: Adaptive oncogenesis of β-catenin emerges from declining liver tissue integrity
item.description: Despite being a common driver of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), oncogenic β-catenin is ineffective at initiating liver cancer on its own. Here the authors show that β-catenin mutations as a single genetic event confer negative fitness in the healthy liver, while driving clonal expansion and tumorigenesis as liver tissue integrity declines with chronic liver disease or aging.

item.title: Nature Communications: Clinical utility of molecular residual disease detection in early-stage resected EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: For patients with resected EGFR-mutated lung cancer, effective strategies to guide post-surgical surveillance remain an unmet need. Here, the author shows that a personalized blood test may indicate molecular residual disease months before radiological progression.

item.title: Nature Communications: Nuclear compartmentalization at the G1/S transition plays a key role in DNA replication control
item.description: The genome is organized into nuclear compartments that correlate with replication timing. Here, the authors show that GINS4 is required for compartment organization at the G1/S transition, which supports DNA replication control, revealing a key role for nuclear architecture in genome duplication.

item.title: Nature Communications: Elevation-structured viral ecological strategies along glacier-fed rivers on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
item.description: Qinghai-Tibet Plateau rivers host microorganisms shaped by climate-sensitive environments. This study shows that viral lifestyles and metabolic functions shift along elevation gradients, influencing microbial dynamics and nutrient cycling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Plasticity of extrachromosomal DNA segregation during drug adaptation
item.description: Extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) carries cancer genes and is thought to segregate randomly, driving heterogeneity within tumors. Here, authors use single-cell tracking to show that some cancer cell clones can actively reconfigure their ecDNA segregation behavior under drug stress to gain resistance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Macrophages tune NK cell IFNγ production through direct lipid transfer
item.description: The metabolic state of NK cells affects their innate immune function, and although cell-intrinsic pathways are better known, their cellular environment could provide cues that are less studied. Here the authors show that in coculture and mouse models, activated macrophages donate membrane lipids and CD36 protein via trogocytosis, which leads to the accumulation of lipid droplets and inhibition of mTORc1 and IFNγ production.

item.title: Nature Communications: Quantitative RNA modification mapping by mass spectrometry with isobaric tags and nucleobase fragment analysis
item.description: The locations and levels of RNA modifications are key to understanding their biological functions. Here, the authors develop proteomics-style, RNA-specific isobaric tandem mass tags for quantitative RNA modification mapping by mass spectrometry, revealing condition-dependent changes and interdependencies among modification pathways.

item.title: Nature Communications: Synthetic cargo adaptors reveal molecular features that enhance dynein activation
item.description: Using in vitro reconstitution and cell-based assays, the authors show that distinct adaptors differentially regulate dynein activity and that the sequence differences between adaptors contribute to the plasticity of dynein motility observed in cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: scAmp enables focal gene amplification analysis from single-cell data
item.description: Oncogene amplification on extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) is associated with poor patient prognosis and drug resistance but can be difficult to detect. Here, the authors describe a new computational tool, single-cell amplicon (“ scAmp ”), which enables the study of ecDNA from single-cell assays.

item.title: Nature Communications: Systematic citywide analysis reveals ecological connectivity of antimicrobial resistance genes across urban water systems
item.description: Despite recent focus on resistance genes in urban wastewater, system-wide studies are still limited. Here, the authors provide genetic evidence across a citywide water system that anthropogenic antibiotic resistance genes might spread from sewage to natural waters and through urban water systems.

item.title: Nature Communications: Benchmarking RNA-seq with the Quartet and MAQC reference materials to establish best practices for accurate alternative splicing analysis
item.description: Alternative splicing detection performance by srRNA-seq lacks systematic benchmarking. Here, the authors assessed isoform- and event-level performance across 42 laboratories and 207 pipelines using large-scale reference datasets, identified key factors, and provided best practices.

item.title: Nature Communications: The RNA helicase domain of NAT10 promotes the biogenesis of hypomodified ribosomes to enhance cancer cell proliferation
item.description: The mechanisms underlying the role of N-acetyltransferase 10 (NAT10) in cancer remain poorly characterised. Here, PROTAC-mediated degradation of NAT10 with a deep mutational scanning assay and functional validation reveal the oncogenic properties of the RNA helicase domain of NAT10.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-wide annotation of human multi-nucleotide variants reveals widespread functional differences from single nucleotide variants
item.description: This work develops MNVAnno for annotating MNVs, systematically analyzes millions of MNVs, and establishes the HumanMNVdb for genetic research.

item.title: Nature Communications: Pan-Ebolavirus nanoparticle vaccine provides protection in rodents from lethal infection by Zaire and Sudan viruses
item.description: This study describes the design and structural characterization of two-component self-assembling nanoparticles co-displaying prefusion Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV) and Sudan ebolavirus (SUDV) glycoprotein antigens with protective capacity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Prenatal PM 2.5 exposure drives epigenetic reprogramming of fetal macrophages linked to atopic dermatitis
item.description: Prenatal exposure to air pollution may shape disease risk later in life. Here, the authors show that epigenetic changes in fetal immune cells persist into later life, promoting inflammatory responses and increasing the risk of atopic dermatitis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Allele-specific chromatin architecture shapes imprinted domains and coordinates a distal enhancer and antisense transcription at the mouse Mest - Copg2 domain
item.description: Here the authors show that parent-specific 3D genome architecture is a common feature of imprinted genes and identify a distal enhancer that works with antisense transcription to regulate neuron-specific imprinting.

item.title: Nature Communications: Human learning of probability distributions is biased toward moderate structural complexity
item.description: Humans build internal models from online observations to adapt to new environments. Here, the authors show that individuals are biased towards building models with moderate structural complexity, regardless of true complexity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Diet-responsive proteogenomic effects following short-term restriction of animal products in humans
item.description: Using longitudinal proteogenomics, the authors reveal diet- and season-sensitive genetic effects on protein abundance linked to cholesterol and methionine metabolism and to immune function.

item.title: Nature Communications: Discovery of a peripheral Myh11-expressing nucleus pulposus cell population demontrating therapeutic potential for disc degeneration
item.description: The authors identify Myh11+ nucleus pulposus cells that maintain disc health throughout life. Their loss accelerates degeneration, while targeting or transplanting them protects, offering a promising regenerative strategy for spinal disorders.

item.title: Nature Communications: MRICombo: a deep-learning-based framework for universal volumetric segmentation grading-staging and malignancy detection across heterogeneous MRI
item.description: Existing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) deep learning models are often task- or sequence-specific. Here, the authors present MRICombo, which segments anatomy, labels tumor types, and supports grading, staging and malignancy detection across heterogeneous sequences.

item.title: Nature Communications: Uncovering the signaling networks of disseminated glioblastoma cells in vivo with INSIGHT
item.description: Glioblastoma recurrence is driven by rare tumor cells that disseminate into the brain, but their signaling programs in vivo are poorly defined. Here, authors develop INSIGHT to map cell-type-specific signaling networks and show that disseminated cells rewire signaling network and global kinase activity toward neuronal and invasion associated pathways.

item.title: Nature Communications: Identification of a membrane transporter for dimethylsulfoniopropionate uptake in marine eukaryotic phytoplankton
item.description: In this study, the authors show that marine eukaryotic phytoplankton widely take up the sulfur compound DMSP via the BCCT family transporter PaDT, suggesting an energy-saving strategy in some taxa and a dual role for phytoplankton as both a source and a sink in organosulfur cycling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-population GWAS meta-analysis identifies bladder cancer susceptibility loci and highlights genetic regulation of smoking-related risk
item.description: This study integrates genetic data from diverse populations to identify 70 loci linked to bladder cancer risk, including 43 novel, and uses experimental approaches to uncover how inherited variation influences this risk in the context of smoking.

item.title: Nature Communications: Targeting m 6 A writer METTL3 with engineered nanovesicles reduces neuroinflammation in vitro and in vivo
item.description: Strategies to modulate neuroinflammation have broad therapeutic potential. Here, the authors develop siMETTL3-hNVs, nanovesicles carrying siRNA targeting METTL3, and show they can reduce neuroinflammation in vitro and in vivo.

item.title: Nature Communications: Healthy vaccinee effect in the evaluation of updated COVID-19 vaccines in elderly populations
item.description: This Swedish population study reveals that healthy vaccinee bias inflates estimates of the effectiveness of updated COVID-19 vaccines in adults aged 65 years or older, highlighting the need to account for frailty and overall health status.

item.title: Nature Communications: Enabling molecular signaling with temperature and ionic-strength independence or programmable dependence
item.description: Environmental factors such as temperature and ionic strength can strongly influence molecular signaling pathways. Here, the authors show that the principle of molecular commutation allows the design of affinity-based networks that either compensate for or exploit these effects, achieving robust or programmable signaling behaviors across diverse computationally modeled systems and a wet-lab-validated DNA logic gate.

item.title: Nature Communications: Non-canonical pore architecture underlies constitutive gating of human retinal TRPM1
item.description: TRPM1 is an ion channel essential for retinal signal transmission and pigmentation. Here, the authors determine the cryo-EM structure of human TRPM1, revealing a non-canonical clockwise pore rotation that underlies its constitutive activity and provides insights into retinal disease mechanisms.

item.title: Nature Communications: Biosynthetic mechanism and ecological function of chirality in Solanum steroidal alkaloids
item.description: Authors investigate the biosynthetic mechanism of steroidal glycoalkaloid (SGA) chirality in Solanum species. GAME8 enzymes are found to catalyze the biosynthesis of R- and S- configured SGAs, which contribute to variations in defense against pests.

item.title: Nature Communications: Nuclear localization of the glutaminyl-tRNA synthetase QARS reveals its role in DNA damage response in ovarian cancer
item.description: Here, the authors find that the glutaminyl-tRNA synthetase QARS, a cytosolic protein involved in mRNA translation, relocates to the nucleus to promote homologous recombination (HR). QARS promotes HR by interacting with SP100 to maintain PML-NB integrity and MRN complex localization, thus reducing tumor sensitivity to treatment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Design of a live-attenuated bacterial vaccine using effector network engineering
item.description: Here, the authors generate an attenuated vaccine of Citrobacter rodentium through systematic reduction and redesign of the effector network, which can potentially serve as a path towards the development of live-attenuated vaccines against diarrhoeal disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Energy-sensing kinase OsSnRK1b and its regulator OsCTK1 promote chilling-induced stomatal closure and cold tolerance
item.description: Here the authors show that OsSnRK1b and OsCTK1 promote stomatal closure and cold survival in rice. This cold tolerance mechanism engages the energy sensing pathway to optimize growth and stress responses according to the environment.

item.title: Nature Communications: A functional atlas of transposon-encoded products and their integration into host networks
item.description: Transposable elements (TEs) are pervasive in host genomes and propagate via self-encoded factors. Here, the authors show that control of TE expression and propagation is deeply embedded within host regulatory circuits.

item.title: Nature Communications: Glycosylation orchestrates megakaryocytic fate of hematopoietic stem cells via Wnt-MUC13 signaling
item.description: This study reveals that B4GALT1-dependent glycosylation programs the bone marrow environment to control hematopoietic stem cell fate, while its loss enhances MUC13–Wnt signaling and disrupts blood production.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bulk delivery of a preassembled apical surface initiates epithelial lumen formation
item.description: Epithelial lumen formation is fundamental to organ development, yet how apical surfaces first emerge remains unclear. Ghosh, Martin, and Chen et al., show that lumen initiation is driven via bulk delivery of a preassembled apical surface, rapidly establishing polarity and luminal identity.

item.title: Nature Communications: DNTTIP2 coordinates RNA exosome activities to ensure fidelity of human ribosome assembly
item.description: Here the authors identify human adaptors of the RNA exosome bound helicase MTR4, linking RNA surveillance to tRNA splicing, pre-mRNA splicing, and ribosome assembly. They show how DNTTIP2 directs processive and distributive activities of the RNA exosome to ensure fidelity of human ribosome assembly.

item.title: Nature Communications: The efficacy, immunogenicity and safety of the LZ901 vaccine for herpes zoster virus in adults 40 years of age or older: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial
item.description: Jingxin Li and colleagues report a randomized, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of LZ901, recombinant gE-Fc fusion protein adjuvanted with aluminium hydroxide, against herpes zoster. They report that the vaccine reduces the risk of viral infection and has favorable safety profiles.

item.title: Nature Communications: CAFs shape the immunosuppressive microenvironment of pancreatic cancer through the Lin28b-STING Axis
item.description: Lin28b is an RNA-binding protein associated with cell transformation and human malignancies. Here, the authors show that Lin28b+ CAFs promote an immunosuppressive microenvironment in pancreatic cancer via inhibition of cGAS-STING signaling.

item.title: Nature Communications: The Plasmodium heme detoxification protein functions in mitochondrial protein synthesis
item.description: Heme biomineralization in malaria parasites was long thought to depend on HDP, a putative heme ligase. Sarrazin et al. show that HDP instead functions as part of the mitochondrial ribosome, influencing parasite viability and drug sensitivity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Standardized chronic disease management reduces comorbidity risk in China
item.description: Using linked health and medical records from 26 million residents in Shenzhen, China, the authors show that enrollment in the national Chronic Disease Patient Management program is associated with lower comorbidity risk among patients newly diagnosed with hypertension or type 2 diabetes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Vulnerability to climate-driven pathogen-specific diarrheal diseases: secondary analysis from the Global Enteric Multicenter Study and Vaccine Impact on Diarrhea in Africa follow-up
item.description: Across the three African countries of The Gambia, Kenya and Mali, Kowalcyk et al identify socio-demographic factors that may mitigate the risks of climate drivers on pathogen-specific diarrheal diseases in young children.

item.title: Nature Communications: PPARα activation overcomes fibroinflammatory liver microenvironment-associated anti-PD-1 resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma by mediating GSDME-dependent pyroptosis
item.description: A fibroinflammatory liver microenvironment (FILM) is prevalent in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and associated with anti-PD-1 resistance. Here the authors show that FILM suppresses GSDME-dependent pyroptosis and drives immune suppression, proposing PPARα activation as a strategy to overcome FILM-associated immune resistance in HCC.

item.title: Nature Communications: MBNL depletion drives stem cell fusion and immature myonuclear states in myotonic dystrophy type 1
item.description: This study shows that muscle stem cells fuse with existing muscle fibres in myotonic dystrophy type 1, producing centrally located nuclei with altered gene-expression states and reshaping diseased muscle.

item.title: Nature Communications: Diagnostic performance of plasma pTau217 in genetically admixed South American populations
item.description: Martino-Adami et al. show that plasma pTau217 accurately identifies Alzheimer’s disease pathology and aligns with clinical diagnosis in admixed South American cohorts, supporting its use where access to cerebrospinal fluid testing is limited.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chrono-atlas of cell-type specific daily gene expression rhythms in the regenerating colon
item.description: How tissues maintain circadian rhythms during regeneration remains poorly understood. Here, the authors generate a 24-hour single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the regenerating mouse colon and show that cells dynamically adapt their circadian programs in a cell-, region-, and injury-dependent manner.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ribosomal architecture and rRNA modification landscape in the tick-borne parasite Babesia divergens
item.description: Babesia microti and B. divergens are tick-borne parasites that are the most prevalent causes of human babesiosis. Here, the authors present cryo-EM structures of ribosomes from B. divergens . Nanopore sequencing reveals distinct rRNA modifications.

item.title: Nature Communications: A critical role of the histone lysine demethylase JmjC1 in regulating severe malaria-associated virulence genes in Plasmodium falciparum
item.description: Severe malaria is linked to upsA var gene expression, whose regulation remains unclear. Here, the authors identify JmjC1 as an epigenetic regulator of upsA var genes at the transcriptional level through chromatin and nuclear organization.

item.title: Nature Communications: α-Synuclein blocks endoplasmic reticulum co-translational protein translocation early in Parkinson’s disease
item.description: Proteomic and transcriptomic profiling on hiPSC-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons with pathological α-synuclein burden reveals defective Sec61A interactions and co-translational translocation of ER-processed proteins.

item.title: Nature Communications: p38β-mediated BiP phosphorylation drives stemness and chemoresistance by suppressing UPR activation in hepatocellular carcinoma
item.description: Tumor-initiating cells drive chemoresistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Here, the authors discover that p38β/MAPK11 phosphorylation of BiP promotes stemness and chemoresistance in HCC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-nucleus analysis of human white adipose tissue reveals adipocyte subsets with distinct metabolic profiles
item.description: Single-nucleus profiling of human adipose tissue reveals low-maturation adipocyte subtypes with pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic signatures linked to metabolic disease and identifies TSHZ3 as a regulator of adipogenesis

item.title: Nature Communications: Non-invasive characterization of perivascular subarachnoid spaces
item.description: Cerebrospinal fluid’s compartmentalization remains unclear. Here, the authors show increased CSF-mobility around major cerebral arteries within the surrounding subarachnoid space, suggesting the presence of distinct CSF spaces in healthy individuals.

item.title: Nature Communications: Vitamin B5 supports anti-PD1 response in HER2-positive gastric cancer and enhances interaction between naïve B cells and T cells
item.description: HER2 + gastric cancer (GC) is commonly treated with immune checkpoint blockade. Here, the authors propose vitamin B5 as potential contributor to naïve B cell function in anti-PD-1-treated GC, finding B5 to be reduced in non-responders and B5 supplementation to improve anti-PD-1 response in a subcutaneous cancer mouse model.

item.title: Nature Communications: Pregnancy promotes tumor metastasis through adenosine-induced immunosuppressive neutrophils in pre-metastatic microenvironment
item.description: Accelerated cancer progression during pregnancy has been previously reported. Here the authors show that adenosine produced in the uterus of pregnant mice promotes tumor metastasis by favouring the accumulation of immunosuppressive neutrophils in the pre metastatic microenvironment.

item.title: Nature Communications: A second yearly booster dose of the VLA15 Lyme borreliosis vaccine candidate in healthy individuals
item.description: Authors show that after 2 or 3 primary doses and a first yearly booster dose, a second yearly booster dose of VLA15, an investigational Lyme disease vaccine, induced robust immune responses among participants 5 − 65 years of age and did not raise safety concerns.

item.title: Nature Communications: Vibrio cholerae -synthesized tryptophan activates innate immune signaling in enteroendocrine cells via phosphorylation of the nuclear receptor ultraspiracle
item.description: Although Vibrio cholerae forms a biofilm in the arthropod intestine, specificity in this interaction has not been demonstrated. Here the authors show that V. cholerae initiates a signaling cascade in host enteroendocrine cells that increases expression of Peritrophin 15a, a host factor that promotes V. cholerae colonization.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-omics integration unravels four molecular subgroups of corticotroph pituitary neuroendocrine tumours with distinct clinicopathological features
item.description: Corticotroph pituitary neuroendocrine tumours (PitNETs)/adenomas are heterogeneous sellar neoplasms that lack molecular-based classification. By performing multi-omics analysis of 270 corticotroph PitNETs, the authors identify four distinct molecular subgroups.

item.title: Nature Communications: Large language models decode narrative pathology reports to define clinically relevant subtypes in IgA nephropathy
item.description: Kidney pathology reports contain rich information that structured assessment does not fully capture. Here, the authors show that large language models extract and standardize it to define reproducible IgA nephropathy subtypes that improve risk prediction and reveal differential treatment responses.

item.title: Nature Communications: Non-enzymatic hepatic ABHD6 interacts with Akt-FoxO1 axis to regulate metabolic health
item.description: Selective hepatic insulin resistance contributes to the development of metabolic disease, but the molecular mechanisms \remain unclear. Here, the authors identify a nonenzymatic role for ABHD6 in promoting selective hepatic insulin resistance through modulation of Akt–FoxO1 signaling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-wide DNA methylation analysis revealed epigenetic mechanism underlying end-stage renal disease
item.description: A two-stage epigenome-wide study identified 52 DNA methylation markers associated with end-stage renal disease across diverse primary kidney diseases, highlighting the shared roles of inflammation, immune dysregulation, and renal fibrosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: A foundation model for sleep-based risk stratification and clinical outcomes
item.description: Clinical sleep studies generate rich physiologic data, yet traditional metrics capture only part of their predictive value. Here, the authors show that a foundation model trained on thousands of recordings learns latent sleep patterns that cluster patients into clinically meaningful risk groups.

item.title: Nature Communications: Corisin induces proteostasis stress to drive epithelial injury and pulmonary fibrosis
item.description: Here, the authors establish the naturally occurring microbiota-derived Corisin as a potent driver of lung injury and fibrosis, revealing a previously unrecognized microbial pathway that disrupts epithelial cell function and promotes pulmonary fibrosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ruxolitinib prevents irreversible autoimmune endocrinopathies in APECED
item.description: APECED is a monogenic autoimmune disorder resulting from deleterious variants in the Autoimmune Regulator gene. Here, the authors report the cases of two patients with APECED in whom early intervention with the JAK1/2 inhibitor ruxolitinib prevented endocrine autoimmunity.

item.title: Nature Communications: High-throughput engineering of bispecific antibodies to enhance macrophage-mediated cytotoxicity of B-cell lymphoma
item.description: B-cell lymphomas can resist macrophage-mediated phagocytosis through different mechanisms. Here the authors present the results of a high-throughput system to screen for antibodies enhancing macrophage-mediated cytotoxicity of B-lymphoma cells, proposing a bispecific antibody comprising a SIRPα decoy domain and a CD38 targeting arm as therapeutic candidate.

item.title: Nature Communications: Deep learning prediction of left atrial structure and function from 12-lead electrocardiograms
item.description: Atrial cardiopathy precedes atrial fibrillation and stroke, yet it is detected through costly, inaccessible cardiac imaging. Here, the authors show that a deep learning model estimates left atrial structure and function from a 12-lead ECG and independently predicts adverse cardiovascular outcomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Early life sugar rationing and ageing related diseases, biological ageing and mortality
item.description: Studies on how early-life nutrition influence ageing are limited. Here, using data from the UK Biobank, the authors find that sugar rationing during early life is associated with a lower incidence of ageing-related diseases and slower aging.

item.title: Nature Communications: A pathogenic CD8⁺ T RM –chemokine axis orchestrates liver fibrosis and provides circulating biomarkers during chronic Clonorchis sinensis infection
item.description: Chronic hepatic parasitic infection drives liver fibrosis. Here the authors establish a pathogenic tissue-resident CD8 + T cell chemokine axis that is linked to liver fibrosis during chronic Clonorchis sinensis infection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Inhaled LTI-03 for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: a randomized dose escalation study
item.description: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and often fatal scarring disease of the lungs with very limited treatment options. Here, the authors show that in a randomized placebo-controlled Phase 1b clinical trial in IPF patients, inhaled LTI-03 was safe and well tolerated. Exploratory analyses showed a reduction in several key proteins driving lung fibrosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: The roles of pre-season immunity, age, viral shedding, and community exposures in shaping influenza household transmission dynamics
item.description: Current understanding of influenza transmission dynamics is limited by lack of information on asymptomatic transmission. Here, the authors use data from a household-based cohort study in South Africa to investigate the relative contribution of viral shedding, pre-existing immunity, and demographic factors on influenza transmission.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cardiovascular outcome of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists vs dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor on end-stage kidney disease patients with heart failure: an emulated target trial in patients with diabetes
item.description: Here the authors provide real-world evidence through a target trial emulation study using the TriNetX federated electronic health record network to show that glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists is associated with a lower risk of the primary composite ischemic cardiovascular events plus heart failure exacerbations compared with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors.

item.title: Nature Communications: Public responses about air quality in the world’s ten most populous countries
item.description: This study analyzes public responses to air pollution in the ten most populous countries, finding that people more exposed to air pollution know less about air quality but have higher concern for it and are more engaged in preventative practices.

item.title: Nature Communications: Effect of a complementary feeding intervention based on iron- and zinc-biofortified pearl millet on the gut microbiota in 12–18-month-old children: a randomized trial
item.description: In this randomized trial, the authors report that biofortified pearl millet is a potentially sustainable, climate-smart, and microbiome-friendly solution to improve micronutrient status in 12−18 month old children.

item.title: Nature Communications: Longitudinal analysis reveals myeloid cell contributions to murine neuroPASC pathogenesis
item.description: While prolonged neuroinflammation is considered a hallmark of Post Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), its basis is poorly understood. The authors here manifest infiltration of peripheral myeloid cells during acute infection and prolonged microglial activation in mice with PASC, potentially contributing to neurological abnormalities.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers reveal transdiagnostic synaptic dysfunction across major psychiatric disorders
item.description: Changes in cerebrospinal fluid synaptic proteins were observed across several psychiatric disorders, including at schizophrenia illness onset. The LAMP1:NPTX2 ratio was linked to psychotic experience, cognitive deficits, and functional impairment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Losartan and prednisolone for post-COVID syndrome and cardiac inflammation: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
item.description: Persistent cardiac symptoms are common in post-COVID syndrome. In the Myoflame-19 trial, losartan plus prednisolone yielded neutral results for the primary outcome, change in left ventricular ejection fraction, in 279 participants with inflammatory cardiac involvement assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Longitudinal characterization of mosaic chromosomal alterations identifies factors influencing clonal dynamics of leukocytes
item.description: Mosaic chromosomal alterations in blood cells increase with age, but their expansion over time varies widely between individuals and genomic regions. Here, the authors analyze longitudinal blood samples to show that chromosomal location, age, smoking status, and links to blood cancer lineages influence clonal expansion, while the influence of inherited susceptibility was limited.

item.title: Nature Communications: An RNase domain-dependent microRNA detection with DNA-spiked nanocage for accurate cancer diagnosis
item.description: Direct measurement of circulating microRNAs in serum without prior amplification remains challenging. Here, the authors develop a fluorescent nanocage platform that directly measures serum microRNAs, which can distinguish samples from patients with lung or gastric cancer from those of healthy donors.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-cell profiling of natural killer/T-cell lymphoma reveals stratified immune features and potential therapeutic implications
item.description: Tumor cell heterogeneity and interactions with the immune microenvironment play a key role in natural killer/T-cell lymphoma (NKTCL). Here, the authors characterize 63 NKTCL samples using single-cell, spatial, and bulk multiomics; they identify four gene expression meta-programs that are associated with tumor proliferation and response to therapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Active conformations of neuronal Na + , K + -ATPase isoforms and a disease-causing mutant
item.description: α 3 Na,K-ATPase is a vital ion pump in neurons. Mutations cause severe neurological diseases. Christensen et al. present functional data and cryo-EM structures obtained at turnover for wild-type and disease mutant Q140L and discuss mechanistic implications.

item.title: Nature Communications: Nanopore sequencing identifies parent-of-origin specific age-associated methylation changes at imprinted loci in the human genome
item.description: DNA methylation changes with age, but parent-of-origin effects remain poorly characterised. Here, the authors use nanopore sequencing to map age-associated methylation across the genome, revealing widespread changes and parent-of-origin-specific aging signatures at imprinted loci.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-omic analysis of androgen-deprived human testes reveals Sertoli cell regulation and niche reprogramming
item.description: Androgens are essential for testis development and male fertility. Here, leveraging androgen-deprived adult human testes as a model, the authors generate a comprehensive multi-omics atlas and uncover molecular mechanisms underlying androgen regulation in the adult human testis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Transcriptomic profiling of human brown and white adipose tissue depots
item.description: White and brown adipose tissues play opposing roles in energy storage and expenditure. Here, the authors show that their transcriptional profiles are more similar within an individual than between anatomically and functionally equivalent depots across different individuals.

item.title: Nature Communications: A distinct CAR-T cell phenotype mediates therapeutic response at limited doses
item.description: Predictors of response to low-yield or low-dose CAR-T cell therapy remain poorly characterized. The authors here show that the therapeutic efficacy and response are associated with absolute numbers of CD27 - CD39 - effector-like CAR-T cells and show that distinct myeloid programs in the pre-manufacturing leukapheresis material influence their generation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Maternal hyperglycemia-induced O -GlcNAcylation of CaMKIIδ promotes mtDNA release and cardiac remodeling in offspring
item.description: The study demonstrates that maternal hyperglycemia activates CaMKIIδ via O-GlcNAcylation, leading to mitochondrial DNA release. Targeting this pathway alleviates cardiac remodeling and identifies circulating mtDNA as a potential biomarker of fetal cardiac injury.

item.title: Nature Communications: B cell CD19 is transferred between immune cells in mice and humans
item.description: Trogocytosis enables the transfer of membrane-bound antigens during pathogenic B-T cell interactions. Here, the authors utilize mouse and human cell models and demonstrate that the B cell marker CD19 is transferred, along with other B cell molecules, to T cells and myeloid cells. Importantly, the transferred molecules can be functional in the receiving cells and serve as a marker for B cell-activated T cells, resulting in a mainly pathogenic phenotype in CNS inflammation”.

item.title: Nature Communications: Restoration of anti-bacterial innate immune cell function lags behind nutritional recovery among children convalescing from complicated severe acute malnutrition
item.description: Children recovering after hospital admission with complicated severe acute malnutrition have a high risk of infectious mortality and morbidity. Here the authors analyse blood samples from a longitudinal cohort of children and show that restoration of innate immune cell function lags behind nutritional recovery over 48 weeks of post-discharge follow up.

item.title: Nature Communications: The OmniAge compendium of aging omic biomarkers links mitotic clocks to clonal hematopoiesis and causality
item.description: OmniAge is a compendium of aging omic biomarkers that reveals previously unknown associations between different biomarker categories. OmniAge, available in R, Python and as a webserver will facilitate discovery of novel biomarker associations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Clonal memory of cell division in humans diverges between healthy haematopoiesis and acute myeloid leukaemia
item.description: Healthy blood stem and progenitor cells display synchronised division across generations — a form of clonal memory lost in AML. A bromodomain inhibitor partially restores it, revealing a potential epigenetic vulnerability in leukaemia.

item.title: Nature Communications: Dynamic remodeling of the pancreas immune landscape in obesity
item.description: Obesity represent predisposition to pancreatic diseases, such as diabetes, pancreatitis and cancer. Here the authors map the pancreatic immune landscape by single cell and spatial transcriptomics and find that in obesity, highly cytotoxic tissue resident memory T-cells in the exocrine pancreas form a dense network around pro-inflammatory macrophages, which changes might lead to chronic inflammation and diseases.

item.title: Nature Communications: Low-burden AI approach for cross-national early identification of cognitive impairment using real-world questionnaire response behaviours
item.description: This study shows that AI can use patterns in how older adults answer routine questionnaires to identify cognitive impairment risk across five countries, supporting low-burden population-level cognitive health monitoring and research.

item.title: Nature Communications: Skeletal muscle properties in long COVID and ME/CFS differ from those induced by bed rest
item.description: Low aerobic capacity in patients with long COVID and ME/CFS is often attributed to physical inactivity. The authors show that long COVID and ME/CFS patients have distinct skeletal muscle changes that cannot be solely explained by physical inactivity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fungal diagnostics and antifungal drug access in Latin America and the Caribbean: an ESCMID EFISG multinational survey
item.description: Here, in a survey of 619 institutions across Latin America and the Caribbean, the authors showcase major gaps in fungal diagnostics and antifungal access, with stark disparities linked to income and institutional capacity, underscoring the urgent need for equitable care.

item.title: Nature Communications: Racial and ethnic disparities in the cause of death for clear cell renal cell carcinoma
item.description: There is inadequate evidence on the trends and contributors of racial and ethnic disparities in causes of death among patients with clear cell renal cell carcinoma. Here the authors report that despite a decreasing trend in mortality, the disparities persist between Black and white people and between Alaska Native and white people with stage, surgery, income, and geographic location identified as potential mediators of the disparities.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fractionated proteomics identifies a protein network mitigating resistance exercise-induced damage in human skeletal muscle
item.description: This study reveals molecular responses of untrained, adapted and deadapted human skeletal muscle to resistance exercise, which identifies a network of mechanosensory proteins and molecular chaperones that ensures skeletal muscle homeostasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: The accumulation of methylglyoxal and acrolein impairs arginine homeostasis causing hyperglycemia and renal abnormalities in male zebrafish
item.description: Reactive carbonyl species contribute to diabetes and its complications. Here the authors used zebrafish lacking both glyoxalase 1 and aldo-keto reductase 1A1A to show carbonyl accumulation and elevated glucose level.

item.title: Nature Communications: The genetics of fibromyalgia and its relationships to psychiatric and medical traits
item.description: The authors conduct genome-wide association studies of fibromyalgia in individuals of European, African, and Latin American ancestries. The findings provide potential targets for future studies to improve diagnosis and treatment of this syndrome.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-fraction or multi-fraction stereotactic ablative body radiotherapy followed by atezolizumab in advanced triple-negative breast cancer: a randomized phase II trial
item.description: Combining radiotherapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors can amplify anti-tumor immune responses. Here the authors report the results of a randomized phase II trial of single fraction or multi-fraction stereotactic ablative body radiotherapy followed by anti-PD-L1 atezolizumab in patients with advanced triple-negative breast cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Large language model driven multicenter prediction and explainable risk attribution of acute kidney injury
item.description: This multicenter study introduces a large language model framework for real-time prediction and explainable risk attribution of acute kidney injury. It has the potential to support early clinical detection and prevention.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cross-species comparative spatial transcriptomics of hair follicle-T cell interactions identifies conserved drivers of cutaneous lupus erythematosus skin disease and associated hair loss
item.description: Cutaneous lupus erythematosus comprises several skin disease subsets, including primary cicatricial alopecia (PCA), characterized by skin inflammation, hair loss and collagen deposition in the follicles. How immune cells contribute to the pathogenesis is controversial. Here, the authors present a comparative spatial transcriptomic analysis of hair follicle-T cell interaction across a CLE/PCA mouse model, pet dog and human biopsies and report an enrichment of CXCR3 + T cells and of B cells in CLE lesional skin as well as changes in CFD and S100 expression.

item.title: Nature Communications: Oncogenic Kras targeting with MRTX1133 or Daraxonrasib specifically synergize with anti-CTLA4 to promote anti-tumor immunity in pancreatic cancer
item.description: Kras mutations have been associated with immune suppression in pancreatic cancer. Here the authors show that KRAS targeting with MRTX1133 or Daraxonrasib specifically synergizes with anti-CTLA4, but not other immune checkpoint inhibitors, in inducing tertiary lymphoid structures and promoting anti-tumor immune responses in preclinical pancreatic cancer models.

item.title: Nature Communications: An ingestible origami-inspired metamaterial for prolonged oral delivery of therapeutics
item.description: Poor adherence to oral drug regimen adversely affects treatments. Here, the authors developed an origami-inspired, oral drug delivery dosage form capable of prolonged residence in the gastric cavity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Host-derived lactic acid disrupts IFN efficacy via antiviral inhibition and proinflammatory amplification
item.description: This study identifies host-produced lactic acid as a critical factor limiting the efficacy of IFN treatment after viral infection. Combining IFN with stiripentol, an approved LDH inhibitor, restores antiviral activity and alleviates inflammation in viral infection models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Personalized Phage Therapy in an ICU Patient with Polymicrobial Pulmonary Infections: a case from a single-arm trial
item.description: This case report presents a patient with sequential pulmonary infections of multidrug resistant (MDR) Acinetobacter baumannii , Klebsiella pneumoniae , and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia , treated with tailored phage therapy adjunctive to antibiotics.

item.title: Nature Communications: Macrophage adenylyl cyclase 7 protects against myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury in male mice
item.description: Excessive inflammation contributes to myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury. Here, the authors show that macrophage ADCY7 suppresses inflammatory signalling, protects against cardiac injury, and represents a potential therapeutic target.

item.title: Nature Communications: Immunological maladaptation preceding spontaneous preterm birth in human pregnancies
item.description: Spontaneous preterm birth often occurs without any clinical warning sign and in the absence of identifiable risk factors. Here, the authors perform a multi-omics analysis of longitudinally collected peripheral blood samples from low-risk pregnancies and identify distinct immune parameters, such as increased adrenergic responsiveness and Th17-skewed CD4 + T cells, that precede idiopathic preterm birth.

item.title: Nature Communications: Inflammatory biomarkers of asymptomatic and symptomatic tuberculosis
item.description: A large number of individuals with tuberculosis (TB) are asymptomatic. Here, the authors characterise blood transcriptomic and proteomic profiles in South African community screening cohorts to identify inflammatory signatures of asymptomatic TB.

item.title: Nature Communications: Low-dose baricitinib plus danazol in primary immune thrombocytopenia: a randomized, controlled phase 2 trial
item.description: Achieving sustained response remains a challenge for patients with difficult-to-treat immune thrombocytopenia (ITP). Here, the authors report that low-dose baricitinib plus danazol may be effective for patients with difficult-to-treat ITP with acceptable safety profiles.

item.title: Nature Communications: ACSS2-KAT5 complex-driven histone crotonylation orchestrates a pro-inflammatory program to promote the transition from MASLD to MASH
item.description: Acetyl-CoA synthetase 2 (ACSS2) is known to regulate lipid metabolism. Here the authors identified ACSS2 drives MASH through nuclear translocation and complexes wiht KAT5 to crotonylate histones and activate AIF1.

item.title: Nature Communications: Trdn-as directs m6A-dependent transcriptional termination for accurate triadin isoform switching, preventing aberrant dyads and cardiomyopathy
item.description: The lncRNA Trdn-as regulates the formation of the cardiac-specific TRDN isoform through transcriptional interference and m6A modification. This is crucial for accurate cardiac dyad calcium release and prevents QT prolongation and cardiomyopathy.

item.title: Nature Communications: A benchmark study of vision and pathology foundation models for computational pathology
item.description: The comparative performance and generalisability of pathology foundation models remain largely unexamined. Here, the authors benchmark 32 AI pathology foundation models across large cancer datasets, showing that generalisation in computational pathology is heterogeneous and task-dependent regardless of dataset scale, but ensemble-based approaches can combine the strengths of different models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cryo-EM structures of biopsy-derived TTR fibrils in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis
item.description: Hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRv) is a fatal autosomal dominant disease characterized by systemic deposition of transthyretin amyloid fibrils. Authors present nineteen high-resolution cryo-EM fibril structures from ten living ATTRv patients carrying nine distinct heterozygous mutations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mitophagy mitigates mitochondrial DNA-induced activation of cGAS-STING in autoimmune thyroiditis
item.description: In this study, the authors demonstrate that mitochondrial DNA leakage activates the cGAS-STING pathway in autoimmune thyroiditis and that restoring mitophagy or pharmacologically inhibiting STING reduces disease severity in mice.
